historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (FY2020-FY2025, C$22,883M -> C$24,468M); equity CAGR is inflated by the C$4.8B MLSE after-tax gain booked to the deficit in 2025, and EPS CAGRs are meaningless (FY2025 EPS 6.79 includes the MLSE gain; FY2024 EPS 0.18 the Bell Media impairments)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS CAGRs (31.6% 3yr, 19.7% 5yr) diverge >30% from revenue (0.4%/1.35%) and equity (1.25%/1.86%) because the endpoints are a C$5.2B disposal gain and a C$2.19B impairment year; neither is operating growth. Owner-FCF (OCF - capex - SBC) CAGR is +0.8% 3yr and -1.5% 5yr: cash generation has not grown in five years while the dividend absorbed more than it, which is the backdrop to the Feb-2025 cut.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (OCF - capex - SBC, C$M): FY2020 3,461; FY2022 3,131; FY2025 3,203. SBC is ~0.4% of revenue and has not grown, so the SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs are essentially identical. Revenue growth across FY2013-FY2025 averaged ~1.5%; the forward base path starts at 2.5% only because Ziply's first full year lands in FY2026.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance delivered, nothing more. Ziply's first full year and the AI data centres carry FY2026-27 revenue to ~2-2.5% growth while Canadian wireless ARPU erodes under a price war in which no carrier wins share; the C$1.5B cost programme roughly offsets that erosion, so the normalised margin edges up only ~0.4pp. Capex spikes on the C$1.7B Saskatchewan build and then settles at a 15% capital intensity as the CRTC wholesale-access mandate makes BCE's own fibre build plateau. Growth fades to the 1.5% the company has averaged for a decade; Bell Media keeps shrinking but is now too small to move the total. Leverage reaches ~3.5x by 2027-28 through asset sales and the halved dividend, not through faster growth.
scenario_narratives.bull: The three new vectors all work. The Canadian wireless price war rationalises within 12-18 months (as the 2017 and 2023 episodes did) and postpaid ARPU recovers; Bell AI Fabric fills the Saskatchewan and Merritt capacity with Cerebras, CoreWeave and Cohere and adds further sovereign-AI contracts; Ziply and the PSP FiberCo scale toward their up-to-8-million US locations with BCE's capital share kept off the balance sheet. Revenue grows 3-3.5% for three years, the C$1.5B savings fall through to a ~43% normalised margin by 2030, capital intensity drops to 14% as Canadian FTTP completes, and a deleveraged BCE earns a 17x terminal FCF multiple with 2% perpetual growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 'race to the bottom' is structural. Three national carriers plus Freedom keep cutting wireless prices with no subscriber winner, the CRTC wholesale fibre regime caps returns on fibre and lets resellers take share on BCE's own network, and Bell Media's linear decline accelerates. Revenue stalls at 0-0.5% after the Ziply annualisation, the normalised margin falls ~1.7pp to 39.5% as cost savings are competed away, capex cannot fall below 16% because Ziply build and AI data-centre maintenance offset the Canadian plateau, and lease costs creep up. Leverage stays near 3.8x, refinancing happens at hybrid-style spreads, and the market pays only 12x terminal FCF for a no-growth, regulated, levered utility-like asset.

valuation_philosophy.summary: BCE is valued as a levered, low-growth, regulated infrastructure operator: unlevered owner FCF after the full lease cash cost, a normalised allowance for the restructuring and working-capital drains that adjusted EBITDA excludes, and the AI data-centre capex spike charged in full, discounted at a CAD WACC that reflects a 60%-debt capital structure. With ~C$41B of senior claims (debt ex-leases, preferreds, NCI) ahead of ~C$26B of common equity, the equity is a thin, leveraged slice of the enterprise: every 1x of terminal FCF multiple is worth roughly C$3.20 (~US$2.25) per share, which is why the terminal cap is the most consequential single assumption and is set below the Gordon-implied multiple in every scenario.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal cap multiple: Gordon at 6.75%/1.5% implies ~19x terminal FCF vs the 15x base cap; equity leverage turns each 1x into ~C$3.20/share.
Wireless price war duration: each 1pp of sustained normalised EBITDA margin is ~C$250M/yr of pre-tax cash, roughly C$3/share in value.
CRTC wholesale fibre mandate: caps returns on new Canadian fibre and could let resellers take share of BCE's own network.
Refinancing: C$4.3B due within one year at Jun-2026 and a growing hybrid layer resetting off GoC + ~240bp; a 50bp WACC move is worth ~C$5/share.
AI data centre execution: C$1.7B committed to a 300 MW Saskatchewan build with two anchor tenants; returns are unproven and the capex is charged in full in every scenario.
Normalised cash drains: the 2.5pp margin allowance for severance and working-capital outflows is a judgment; if BCE's restructuring genuinely ends after 2028, base value rises.

inputs.share_count_basis: Q2-2026 FS: weighted average basic = diluted = 932.5M for Q1 and Q2 2026 (no dilutive securities). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and settled by on-market purchases (C$216M FY2025, C$95M H1-2026). DRIP treasury issuance lifted the count 912.3M -> 932.5M during 2025 but the count has not moved in 2026, so no further non-SBC issuance is modelled.
inputs.sbc_source: Metrics.csv StockBasedComp FY2025 (C$90M; Q1-26 41, Q2-26 19). Canadian filer: no net-share-settlement tax withholding (EquityAwardTaxes = 0); awards are settled with shares bought on market (C$216M FY2025), which is the cash mechanism holding the count flat.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows are CAD; the valuation is quoted against the NYSE listing (Yahoo 'BCE', USD), which is the listing refresh_price.py tracks. CAD->USD 0.702 from Yahoo CADUSD=X at 2026-10-02T21:18Z. Parity check against the TSX line: BCE.TO C$28.17 x 0.702 = US$19.78 vs NYSE US$19.73 at the same close, a 0.2% tie, confirming rate, direction and quote basis. CAD per-share twins are emitted alongside the USD canonical values; the rate is not refreshed by refresh_price.py and should be re-dated with each price refresh.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CAD. Risk-free: Government of Canada 10y ~3.4%. Cost of equity ~10% (levered beta ~1.1 on a ~5.5% Canadian ERP; equity is only ~37% of the capital structure). Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (2026 issues: M-68 4.40% 2033, M-69 4.70% 2036, M-70 5.30% 2056; junior subordinated hybrids 5.375%/5.875%), after-tax ~3.7% at 26.5%. Preferred shares ~6%. Market weights: equity C$26.3B (932.5M x C$28.17), debt ex-leases C$37.5B, preferreds C$3.2B -> ~39/56/5 -> ~6.3%. Set at 6.75% because roughly half the incremental funding is now sub-investment-grade hybrid paper that resets off GoC + ~240bp, and refinancing of the 2027-2030 tower will be at today's spreads, not the embedded coupon. The regulatory (CRTC wholesale fibre) and wireless price-war risk is carried in the scenario flows and the 30% bear weight, NOT in the discount rate, so it is charged once. Same WACC in every scenario.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. BCE reports lease liabilities inside 'Debt due within one year' and 'Long-term debt' and pays principal through financing, so reported OCF and BCE's own FCF exclude ~C$1.1B/yr of lease principal. The model charges the full lease cash cost (FY2025 principal C$1,127M + lease interest C$194M = C$1,321M, 5.4% of revenue; H1-2026 principal run-rate ~C$1.0B/yr, so 4.8% forward) via lease_cost_pct_path, and EXCLUDES the C$4,309M lease liability (FY2025 FS line 759; the latest disclosed balance, used for Jun-2026) from total_debt. da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 D&A 5,238 less ROU depreciation 874 = 4,364, 17.8% of revenue), so cash-tax EBIT does not charge the lease twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100% of subsidiaries' EBITDA). NCI charged once, in the equity bridge, at ~11x its annualised share of earnings (FY2025 C$54M, H1-2026 C$48M -> ~C$95M/yr) = C$1,000M, rather than its C$314M book value.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table: non-US operating company with material leases, NCI, preferred shares and a CAD-filing / USD-quote split -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). BCE is an operating telecom, not a bank/REIT/holdco; its debt is real financial debt, so an unlevered DCF on WACC less net debt is the right frame. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry, no prior DCF). EARNINGS BASE: adjusted EBITDA and cash flows, never GAAP net income: FY2024 NI (C$163M attributable) is depressed by C$2.19B Bell Media impairments and FY2025 NI (C$6.3B) is inflated by the C$5.2B MLSE disposal gain; both are excluded. FY0 = FY2025 actual (revenue C$24,468M, adjusted EBITDA C$10,658M, 43.6%), with only 5 months of Ziply Fiber (closed 2025-08-01), so FY2026 growth carries ~2pp of acquisition annualisation. EBITDA MARGIN DRIVER is defined as adjusted EBITDA + SBC (BCE's adjusted EBITDA is already after SBC; adding it back keeps SBC visible as its own line) LESS a normalised ~2.5% of revenue for the cash drains BCE's adjusted EBITDA excludes but its FCF bears every year: severance/restructuring paid (C$330M FY2024, C$425M FY2025), acquisition costs, and the persistent negative change in operating assets/liabilities (-C$534M, -C$657M). Calibration: FY2026 base flow ~C$3.1B unlevered after leases and the C$1.3B Saskatchewan AI data-centre capex; on BCE's own definition (levered, before lease principal, after pref/NCI dividends) that maps to ~C$2.7B including the data centre, vs guidance C$3.3-3.5B which, by management's own funding commentary ('potential debt financings' for the ~C$1.7B data-centre build), sits largely outside it. So the model is mildly conservative against guidance, deliberately. REPORTED_FCF = OCF - capex (C$6,993M - C$3,700M); last_fcf = reported - SBC; after lease principal it is ~C$2.08B, and that lease-inclusive basis is what the forward build uses. INTEREST INCOME (C$79M FY2025) is not stripped: BCE is ~C$37B net debt, not net cash. EQUITY BRIDGE: preferred shares C$3,216M (Jun-2026 book; first-loss-ahead-of-common claim) and NCI C$1,000M deducted; investments in associates/JVs C$1,509M added (Montreal Canadiens 20.2% stake reclassified at C$965M fair value in Q1 2026, plus other associates; their equity income is not in EBITDA, so no double count). Hybrids (C$1.5B Series D/E Feb-2026 plus 2025 issues) are counted 100% as debt, unlike the agencies' and BCE's 50% equity credit. NOT IN THE BRIDGE, deliberately: the C$675M land-mobile-radio sale to Motorola (expected Q4 2026; its EBITDA is still in the flows, so the swap is roughly value-neutral), and the C$3.6B net pension surplus (benefit assets 4,744 less obligations 1,115) -- its value already flows through as near-zero cash contributions (C$27M H1-2026), so adding the stock would count it twice. BUYBACKS: BCE buys shares only to settle share-based awards (C$216M FY2025); the flat count is funded, not a convention. Historical CAGRs deliberately not used as the forward base: FY2013-era growth predates Ziply, the CRTC wholesale-fibre ruling (Aug 2025) and the 2026 wireless price war.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 2.5% sits inside the 1-5% guide and matches H1-2026 (+2.7%), almost all of it Ziply annualisation; organic Canada is ~flat under the wireless price war. 2027 2.0% adds phase 1 of the Saskatchewan AI data centre (Cerebras, CoreWeave; online H1 2027) and Merritt phase 2. Glides to 1.5%, the FY2013-2025 trend, as Canadian fibre build 'plateaus' under the CRTC wholesale mandate and Bell Media keeps shrinking.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Company adjusted EBITDA margin 43.6% FY2025; guide 0-4% EBITDA growth vs 1-5% revenue implies ~43.3% FY2026. Driver = company margin + 0.37pp SBC - 2.5pp normalised severance/acquisition-cost/working-capital drain. Base lets the C$1.5B-by-2028 cost programme only offset price-war ARPU erosion and the lower-margin AI/Ateko and Ziply mix: +0.4pp by 2029, then flat.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 19.5% = core <15% capital-intensity guide plus ~C$1.3B Saskatchewan data-centre spend in H2 (H1 already 15.6%). FY2027 16.5% carries the remaining ~C$0.4B. Then 15.0%, inside BCE's own target and below the 16-17% FY2013-2024 history, because Canadian FTTP expansion is slowing; Ziply's 68% capital intensity is ~4% of revenue and FiberCo is funded off balance sheet with PSP.
base.da_rationale: Ex right-of-use D&A: H1-2026 annualised (2,732 x 2 less ~880 ROU) = ~18.3% of revenue, elevated by Ziply customer-relationship amortisation. Converges toward capex (15.5%) over the decade so the terminal tax shield is not perpetuated.
base.tax_rationale: Unlevered cash tax on EBIT (interest shield sits in WACC). FY2025 cash taxes C$737M ex-divestiture ~22% of the comparable EBIT base, flattered by accelerated CCA (Accelerated Investment Incentive phasing out) and fibre/spectrum timing; ramps to 26%, between the 26.5% Canadian combined rate and US Ziply. The C$542M Q1-2026 tax on the MLSE gain is a divestiture item and excluded.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30% (above the 15% default): a single-regulator dependency (CRTC wholesale fibre, upheld by the Minister in Aug 2025), a sector-wide price war TD calls unprecedented in 30 years, and ~3.8x leverage with sub-investment-grade hybrid tranches mean the downside path is both plausible and already partly in evidence (H1-2026 FCF -5.3%). Base 50%: guidance has been reaffirmed and is being met. Bull 20% (below the 35% default): it needs three independent things to go right at once -- price-war de-escalation, AI data-centre contracts beyond the anchor tenants, and Ziply/FiberCo execution after an early subscriber-count restatement.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
